question.text: This company, based in Amsterdam, was given a monopoly on Dutch spice trade in 1602 and was one of the first major international corporations.
question.answerHtml: Dutch East India Company [accept United East Indian Company]
question.clue: It exported pepper from the Malukus, but was unable to displace Portuguese sandalwood traders from Timor.

swap.text: Prior to World War II and Japanese Invasion, Indonesia was a colonial holding of this European country. This country's capital of Amsterdam is home to many speakers of the Dutch language.
swap.clue: One military operation in this country was likely betrayed by a double agent nicknamed 'King Kong', leading to the destruction of much of the British 1st Airborne Division.

question.leadin: This European country's colonial holdings included the Congo Free State, where enslaved workers had their hands cut off if they couldn't harvest enough of a certain crop.
question.text: Name this country. Originally, its King Leopold II personally owned the Congo and authorized the Force Publique to commit atrocities to protect his investments.
question.clue: One-third of the votes cast in an election in this country set up by the provisional government of Charles Rogier were left blank in protest.

swap.text: This operation attempted to capture bridges in the Netherlands using paratroopers and saw the British First Airborne Division meet heavier opposition than planned while trying to cross the Rhine River, crushing Allied hopes of ending the war by Christmas of 1944.
swap.clue: It was the last attempt to win the war by Christmas and had a strategic objective of forcing a crossing of the at .

question.leadin: This conflict was stalled for 12 years until the outbreak of the Thirty Years' War.
question.text: Name this war in which William of Orange was successful in overthrowing Habsburg rule over the Netherlands.
question.answerHtml: Eighty Years’ War (prompt on things like “Dutch War of Independence”)
question.clue: Italian engineer Frederico Giambelli helped design fire ships during this war, during which Balthasar Gerard assassinated a leader.

swap.leadin: Federigo Giambelli designed specialized fireships called "hellburners" to defend this city.
swap.text: Name this Low Countries city which was sacked during an event known as the "Spanish Fury."
swap.clue: Echoing Rome, the people of this city affixed the letters SPQA to its pioneering Beurs building.

question.text: The Eighty Years' War is considered to be a War of Independence for this modern-day nation with capital at Amsterdam.
question.clue: This country used a defensive Water Line to halt an invasion in its "disaster year," during which a new stadtholder was chosen.

swap.leadin: A rejected 1937 law in this country was derisively nicknamed the Maulkuerfgesetz, or the "muzzle law," and sought to outlaw the Communist Party.
swap.text: Name this "Gibraltar of the North" which helps to name a European zone with Belgium and the Netherlands.
swap.clue: Known as the Gibraltar of the North, this nation's fortifications were improved upon by Vauban under Louis XIV.

question.text: Maurice and William were members of this Dutch house's Nassau branch, whose William III was installed in the Glorious Revolution. It is named for a principality rather than a color.
question.clue: Safety regulations require the use of white alternating with this color in certain tower structures, such as the Yerevan TV Tower and the Tokyo Tower.

swap.leadin: Julie Wheelwright claimed this woman's performances of supposed Javanese religious rituals led her to be viewed as a "nude of art."
swap.text: Name this exotic dancer who, after being identified by French intelligence as "H-21," was executed in 1917 for espionage.
swap.answerHtml: Mata Hari [or Margaretha Geertruida Zelle; or Margaretha Geertruida MacLeod]
swap.clue: This person adopted a Malay name that meant "eye of the day" as a stage name.

question.leadin: At this battle, the attacking force under Robert II of Artois was defeated by William of Julich.
question.text: Name this 1302 battle at which French knights were decisively beaten by Flemish militia, making it an example of the nascent "Infantry Revolution."
question.answerHtml: Battle of the Golden Spurs [or Battle of Courtrai]
question.clue: Stories of folk heroes who fought in this battle, such as the Cistercian lay brother Willem van Saeftinghe ("VILL-uhm vahn SAHF-ting-uh") and the weaver Pieter de Coninck, are romanticized in a novel by Hendrik Conscience ("kon-s'YAWNSS").

swap.leadin: Adam Hochschild wrote a book about the "Ghost" of a ruler of this name whose policies were exposed by the Casement Report.
swap.text: Give this name of several kings, the second of whom personally owned the Congo Free State.
swap.clue: Atrocities committed under a king of this name were detailed in the Casement Report which included accounts of his Force Publique severing the limbs of workers who failed to meet rubber quotas.

question.leadin: During the French Revolutionary Wars, this region lent its name to a campaign that included the Battle of Caesar's Camp.
question.text: Name this region that gives its name to a 1792 to 1795 campaign during the War of the First Coalition. This region's port of Bruges ("broozh") historically traded wool with England.
question.answerHtml: Flanders [or Vlaaanderen; or Flandre; or Flandern; accept Flanders Campaign; accept West Flanders; accept East Flanders; accept County of Flanders; prompt on Belgium]
question.clue: A shibboleth was used here prior to the Battle of the Golden Spurs, and parts of the "race to the sea" occurred here, ending after the opening of the sea-locks during the Battle of the Yser.

swap.text: This University of Leuven scholar, who created a 1569 world map, led the "golden age of Netherlandish cartography." This engraver, who coined the term "atlas," names a widely-used but controversial map "projection."
swap.clue: This Flemish geographer created a 1569 world map that represented sailing courses as straight lines and distorted Greenland to the size of Africa.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the Netherlands before independence.
question.text: Stadtholders were often members of this house. Members of this house included William the Silent, leader at the onset of the Dutch Revolt, and William III, who ascended to the throne of England in the Glorious Revolution.
question.clue: A group supported by this dynasty that adopted crescent-shaped symbols for Ottoman support was the Sea Beggars.

swap.leadin: J. L. Motley originated the phrase "when he died, the little children cried" in a discussion of this man, the first victim of an assassination by handgun.
swap.text: Name this ruler, who was aided in a rebellion by the Sea Beggars. He founded a new royal house after inheriting a title from Rene de Chalon ("shah-LON").
swap.answerHtml: William the Silent [or William I or William of Orange or William the Taciturn or Willem van Oranje or Willem de Zwigjer; prompt on William or Willem]
swap.clue: This leader's main antagonist dubbed this person a "pest on the whole of Christianity" and offered a massive bounty on this person's head, which led to the first assassination of a head of state with a firearm.

question.leadin: This man authored tracts like Defenso Fidei and De Imperio where he argued for the right of Holland to determine its own religious affairs.
question.text: Identify this "Miracle of Holland" who escaped from a life sentence at Loevestein after his wife smuggled him out of captivity in a book chest.
question.clue: This Dutch thinker and author of On the Laws of War and Peace is considered one of the founders of International Law.

swap.leadin: Near the end of the Eighty Years' War a Spanish fleet carrying troops to Flanders was overtaken by a Dutch fleet of only eighteen ships, which forced the Spanish to withdraw to the neutral waters of England; a month later, the rest of the Dutch broke neutrality and destroyed the Spanish.
swap.text: Name this battle of October 21, 1639, which broke the naval power of Spain and made the reputation of the winning admiral.

question.leadin: This action was caused when unpaid mercenaries decided to loot the central city and it stiffened Dutch resistance, hastening the signing of the Pacification of Ghent.
question.text: Name this 1576 massacre often referred to as the Spanish Fury.
question.clue: Otto Oberstein, drowned in the Scheldt while retreating from it, and the five thousand troops under the Marquis de Havre mostly failed to offer any resistance.

swap.text: The Dutch were led by this Grand Pensionary whose brother Cornelis accompanied the fleet at Medway.
swap.clue: In order to focus on his country's invasion in the War of Devolution, this man quickly negotiated the Treaty of Breda to end a war with England.
